items.text:
गवां बन्धनयोक्त्रेषु भवेन्मृत्युरकामतः ।
अकामकृतपापस्य प्रायश्चित्तं कथं भवेत् ॥ ८.१ ॥
items.tr:
gavāṃ bandhanayoktreṣu bhavenmṛtyurakāmataḥ |
akāmakṛtapāpasya prāyaścittaṃ kathaṃ bhavet || 8.1 ||
items.en: If a cow dies by accident while tied with ropes or yoke-straps, how should a person atone for a sin he did not intend?

items.text:
वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषां धर्मशास्त्रं विजानताम् ।
स्वकर्मरतविप्राणां स्वकं पापं निवेदयेत् ॥ ८.२ ॥
items.tr:
vedavedāṅgaviduṣāṃ dharmaśāstraṃ vijānatām |
svakarmarataviprāṇāṃ svakaṃ pāpaṃ nivedayet || 8.2 ||
items.en: He should confess his sin to Brahmins who know the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, understand the dharmaśāstra, and are devoted to their own duties.
items.note: Vedāṅga: the six 'limbs' or helper sciences of the Veda (phonetics, ritual, grammar, word-meaning, metre, astronomy). Dharmaśāstra: the texts on religious and social law.

items.text:
सावित्र्याश्चापि गायत्र्याः संध्योपास्त्यग्निकार्ययोः ।
अज्ञानात्कृषिकर्तारो ब्राह्मणा नामधारकाः ॥ ८.३ ॥
items.tr:
sāvitryāścāpi gāyatryāḥ saṃdhyopāstyagnikāryayoḥ |
ajñānātkṛṣikartāro brāhmaṇā nāmadhārakāḥ || 8.3 ||
items.en: Brahmins who do not know the Sāvitrī and Gāyatrī, nor the sandhyā worship and the fire rites, and who live by farming, are Brahmins in name only.
items.note: Gāyatrī (also called Sāvitrī): the most sacred Vedic verse, recited daily. Sandhyā: the daily prayers at dawn, noon and dusk.

items.text:
अव्रतानां अमन्त्राणां जातिमात्रोपजीविनाम् ।
सहस्रशः समेतानां परिषत्त्वं न विद्यते ॥ ८.४ ॥
items.tr:
avratānāṃ amantrāṇāṃ jātimātropajīvinām |
sahasraśaḥ sametānāṃ pariṣattvaṃ na vidyate || 8.4 ||
items.en: Men who keep no vows, know no mantras and live only on the strength of their birth do not form a valid pariṣad, even if thousands of them gather.
items.note: Pariṣad: a council of learned Brahmins that decides the correct atonement.

items.text:
यद्वदन्ति तमोमूढा मूर्खा धर्मं अतद्विदः ।
तत्पापं शतधा भूत्वा तद्वक्तॄनधिगच्छति ॥ ८.५ ॥
items.tr:
yadvadanti tamomūḍhā mūrkhā dharmaṃ atadvidaḥ |
tatpāpaṃ śatadhā bhūtvā tadvaktṝnadhigacchati || 8.5 ||
items.en: Whatever such dull fools, who do not know dharma, declare to be dharma, that sin grows a hundredfold and falls on those who declared it.

items.text:
अज्ञात्वा धर्मशास्त्राणि प्रायश्चित्तं ददाति यः ।
प्रायश्चित्ती भवेत्पूतः किल्बिषं पर्षदि व्रजेत् ॥ ८.६ ॥
items.tr:
ajñātvā dharmaśāstrāṇi prāyaścittaṃ dadāti yaḥ |
prāyaścittī bhavetpūtaḥ kilbiṣaṃ parṣadi vrajet || 8.6 ||
items.en: If someone prescribes an atonement without knowing the dharma texts, the person who performs it becomes pure, but the sin passes to the council.

items.text:
चत्वारो वा त्रयो वापि यं ब्रूयुर्वेदपारगाः ।
स धर्मेति विज्ञेयो नेतरैस्तु सहस्रशः ॥ ८.७ ॥
items.tr:
catvāro vā trayo vāpi yaṃ brūyurvedapāragāḥ |
sa dharmeti vijñeyo netaraistu sahasraśaḥ || 8.7 ||
items.en: What four, or even three, masters of the Vedas declare should be accepted as dharma, not what thousands of others say.

items.text:
प्रमाणमार्गं मार्गन्तो ये धर्मं प्रवदन्ति वै ।
तेषां उद्विजते पापं सद्भूतगुणवादिनाम् ॥ ८.८ ॥
items.tr:
pramāṇamārgaṃ mārganto ye dharmaṃ pravadanti vai |
teṣāṃ udvijate pāpaṃ sadbhūtaguṇavādinām || 8.8 ||
items.en: Sin shrinks in fear from those who declare dharma by following the path of proper authority and who speak of true virtues.

items.text:
यथाश्मनि स्थितं तोयं मारुतार्केण शुध्यति ।
एवं परिषदादेशान्नाशयेत्तस्य दुष्कृतं ॥ ८.९ ॥
items.tr:
yathāśmani sthitaṃ toyaṃ mārutārkeṇa śudhyati |
evaṃ pariṣadādeśānnāśayettasya duṣkṛtaṃ || 8.9 ||
items.en: Just as water standing on a rock is dried away by wind and sun, so the wrongdoer's sin is destroyed by the council's ruling.

items.text:
नैव गच्छति कर्तारं नैव गच्छति पर्षदम् ।
मारुतार्कादिसम्योगात्पापं नश्यति तोयवत् ॥ ८.१० ॥
items.tr:
naiva gacchati kartāraṃ naiva gacchati parṣadam |
mārutārkādisamyogātpāpaṃ naśyati toyavat || 8.10 ||
items.en: The sin goes neither to the doer nor to the council. Like water touched by wind and sun, it simply disappears.

items.text:
चत्वारो वा त्रयो वापि वेदवन्तोऽग्निहोत्रिणः ।
ब्राह्मणानां समर्था ये परिषत्साभिधीयते ॥ ८.११ ॥
items.tr:
catvāro vā trayo vāpi vedavanto'gnihotriṇaḥ |
brāhmaṇānāṃ samarthā ye pariṣatsābhidhīyate || 8.11 ||
items.en: Four or three capable Brahmins who know the Vedas and keep the agnihotra are called a council.
items.note: Agnihotra: the twice-daily offering into the sacred household fire kept by a householder.

items.text:
अनाहिताग्नयो येऽन्ये वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः ।
पञ्च त्रयो वा धर्मज्ञाः परिषत्सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ ८.१२ ॥
items.tr:
anāhitāgnayo ye'nye vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ |
pañca trayo vā dharmajñāḥ pariṣatsā prakīrtitā || 8.12 ||
items.en: Or five or three others who do not keep the sacred fires but have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas and know dharma, are also called a council.

items.text:
मुनीनां आत्मविद्यानां द्विजानां यज्ञयाजिनाम् ।
वेदव्रतेषु स्नातानां एकोऽपि परिषद्भवेत् ॥ ८.१३ ॥
items.tr:
munīnāṃ ātmavidyānāṃ dvijānāṃ yajñayājinām |
vedavrateṣu snātānāṃ eko'pi pariṣadbhavet || 8.13 ||
items.en: Among sages who know the Self, twice-born men who perform sacrifices, and those who have completed their Vedic vows and the closing bath, even a single person can be a council.
items.note: Twice-born (dvija): men of the top three varṇas (Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya) who have had the sacred-thread rite.

items.text:
पञ्च पूर्वं मया प्रोक्तास्तेषां चासंभवे त्रयः ।
स्ववृत्तिपरितुष्टो ये परिषत्सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ ८.१४ ॥
items.tr:
pañca pūrvaṃ mayā proktāsteṣāṃ cāsaṃbhave trayaḥ |
svavṛttiparituṣṭo ye pariṣatsā prakīrtitā || 8.14 ||
items.en: I said five before; if five cannot be found, then three, who are content with their own proper way of life, are called a council.

items.text:
अत ऊर्ध्वं तु ये विप्राः केवलं नामधारकाः ।
परिषत्त्वं न तेष्वस्ति सहस्रगुणितेष्वपि ॥ ८.१५ ॥
items.tr:
ata ūrdhvaṃ tu ye viprāḥ kevalaṃ nāmadhārakāḥ |
pariṣattvaṃ na teṣvasti sahasraguṇiteṣvapi || 8.15 ||
items.en: Other than these, Brahmins who only carry the name do not make a council, even if there are a thousand times as many.

items.text:
यथा काष्ठमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः ।
ब्राह्मणस्त्वनधीयानस्त्रयस्ते नामधारकाः ॥ ८.१६ ॥
items.tr:
yathā kāṣṭhamayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ |
brāhmaṇastvanadhīyānastrayaste nāmadhārakāḥ || 8.16 ||
items.en: Like an elephant made of wood or a deer made of leather, a Brahmin who has not studied the Veda: these three carry only the name.

items.text:
ग्रामस्थानं यथा शून्यं यथा कूपस्तु निर्जलः ।
यथा हुतं अनग्नौ च अमन्त्रो ब्राह्मणस्तथा ॥ ८.१७ ॥
items.tr:
grāmasthānaṃ yathā śūnyaṃ yathā kūpastu nirjalaḥ |
yathā hutaṃ anagnau ca amantro brāhmaṇastathā || 8.17 ||
items.en: Like an empty village site, a well without water, or an offering poured where there is no fire, so is a Brahmin without mantras.

items.text:
यथा षण्ढोऽफलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौरूषराफला ।
यथा चाज्ञेऽफलं दानं तथा विप्रोऽनृचोऽफलः ॥ ८.१८ ॥
items.tr:
yathā ṣaṇḍho'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaurūṣarāphalā |
yathā cājñe'phalaṃ dānaṃ tathā vipro'nṛco'phalaḥ || 8.18 ||
items.en: As a eunuch is fruitless with women, as salty barren land gives no crop, and as a gift to an ignorant man brings no fruit, so a Brahmin who does not know the Vedic verses is fruitless.
items.note: 'gaur ūṣarā' is read here as barren saline land; it could also mean a barren cow.

items.text:
चित्रकर्म यथानेकैरङ्गैरुन्मील्यते शनैः ।
ब्राह्मण्यं अपि तद्वद्धि संस्कारैर्मन्त्रपुर्वकैः ॥ ८.१९ ॥
items.tr:
citrakarma yathānekairaṅgairunmīlyate śanaiḥ |
brāhmaṇyaṃ api tadvaddhi saṃskārairmantrapurvakaiḥ || 8.19 ||
items.en: Just as a painting is slowly brought out by many strokes, Brahminhood too is brought out by saṃskāras done with mantras.
items.note: Saṃskāra: a life-cycle rite of purification (birth, sacred thread, marriage and so on).

items.text:
प्रायश्चित्तं प्रयच्छन्ति ये द्विजा नामधारकाः ।
ते द्विजा पापकर्माणः समेता नरकं ययुः ॥ ८.२० ॥
items.tr:
prāyaścittaṃ prayacchanti ye dvijā nāmadhārakāḥ |
te dvijā pāpakarmāṇaḥ sametā narakaṃ yayuḥ || 8.20 ||
items.en: Twice-born men who are so in name only and who still prescribe atonements are sinners; together they go to hell.

items.text:
ये पठन्ति द्विजा वेदं पञ्चयज्ञरताश्च ये ।
त्रैलोक्यं तारयन्त्येते पञ्चेन्द्रियरता अपि ॥ ८.२१ ॥
items.tr:
ye paṭhanti dvijā vedaṃ pañcayajñaratāśca ye |
trailokyaṃ tārayantyete pañcendriyaratā api || 8.21 ||
items.en: Twice-born men who recite the Veda and are devoted to the five great sacrifices save all three worlds, even if they enjoy the pleasures of the senses.
items.note: Five great sacrifices (pañca-mahāyajña): daily duties to the Veda, the gods, the ancestors, living beings and guests.

items.text:
संप्रणीतः श्मशानेषु दीप्तोऽग्निः सर्वभक्षकः ।
एवं च वेदविद्विप्रः सर्वभक्षोऽपि दैवतं ॥ ८.२२ ॥
items.tr:
saṃpraṇītaḥ śmaśāneṣu dīpto'gniḥ sarvabhakṣakaḥ |
evaṃ ca vedavidvipraḥ sarvabhakṣo'pi daivataṃ || 8.22 ||
items.en: A fire lit in the cremation ground eats everything and stays pure; in the same way a Brahmin who knows the Veda is like a god, even if he eats anything.

items.text:
अमेध्यानि तु सर्वाणि प्रक्षिप्यन्ते यथोदके ।
तथैव किल्बिषं सर्वं प्रक्षिपेच्च द्विजानले ॥ ८.२३ ॥
items.tr:
amedhyāni tu sarvāṇi prakṣipyante yathodake |
tathaiva kilbiṣaṃ sarvaṃ prakṣipecca dvijānale || 8.23 ||
items.en: Just as all impure things are thrown into water, so one should throw all one's sin into the fire that is the Brahmin.

items.text:
गायत्रीरहितो विप्रः शूद्रादप्यशुचिर्भवेत् ।
गायत्रीब्रह्मतत्त्वज्ञाः संपूज्यन्ते जनैर्द्विजाः ॥ ८.२४ ॥
items.tr:
gāyatrīrahito vipraḥ śūdrādapyaśucirbhavet |
gāyatrībrahmatattvajñāḥ saṃpūjyante janairdvijāḥ || 8.24 ||
items.en: A Brahmin without the Gāyatrī becomes more impure even than a Śūdra. Twice-born men who know the Gāyatrī and the truth of Brahman are honoured by people.

items.text:
दुःशीलोऽपि द्विजः पूज्यो न तु शूद्रो जितेन्द्रियः ।
कः परित्यज्य गां दुष्टां दुहेच्छीलवतीं खरीं ॥ ८.२५ ॥
items.tr:
duḥśīlo'pi dvijaḥ pūjyo na tu śūdro jitendriyaḥ |
kaḥ parityajya gāṃ duṣṭāṃ duhecchīlavatīṃ kharīṃ || 8.25 ||
items.en: A twice-born man should be honoured even if his conduct is bad, but not a Śūdra even if he has controlled his senses. Who would leave a bad-tempered cow to milk a well-behaved donkey?

items.text:
धर्मशास्त्ररथारूढा वेदखड्गधरा द्विजाः ।
क्रीडार्थं अपि यद्ब्रूयुः स धर्मः परमः स्मृतः ॥ ८.२६ ॥
items.tr:
dharmaśāstrarathārūḍhā vedakhaḍgadharā dvijāḥ |
krīḍārthaṃ api yadbrūyuḥ sa dharmaḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ || 8.26 ||
items.en: Twice-born men who ride the chariot of the dharmaśāstra and hold the sword of the Veda: whatever they say, even in jest, is held to be the highest dharma.

items.text:
चातुर्वेद्यो विकल्पी च अङ्गविद्धर्मपाठकः ।
त्रयश्च आश्रमो मुख्याः पर्षदेषा दशावरा ॥ ८.२७ ॥
items.tr:
cāturvedyo vikalpī ca aṅgaviddharmapāṭhakaḥ |
trayaśca āśramo mukhyāḥ parṣadeṣā daśāvarā || 8.27 ||
items.en: Four men who know the Vedas, one skilled in reasoning, one who knows the Vedāṅgas, one who teaches dharma, and three from the main stages of life: this council has no fewer than ten members.
items.note: The first word (cāturvedya) is unclear: it may mean four Vedic scholars or one who knows all four Vedas. Read as four, the list adds up to ten.

items.text:
राज्ञश्चानुमते स्थित्वा प्रायश्चित्तं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
स्वयं एव न कर्तव्यं कर्तव्या स्वल्पनिष्कृतिः ॥ ८.२८ ॥
items.tr:
rājñaścānumate sthitvā prāyaścittaṃ vinirdiśet |
svayaṃ eva na kartavyaṃ kartavyā svalpaniṣkṛtiḥ || 8.28 ||
items.en: The council should prescribe atonement only with the king's consent. It should not act on its own, except to give a minor atonement.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणांस्तानतिक्रम्य राजा कर्तुं यदिच्छति ।
तत्पापं शतधा भूत्वा राजानं अनुगच्छति ॥ ८.२९ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇāṃstānatikramya rājā kartuṃ yadicchati |
tatpāpaṃ śatadhā bhūtvā rājānaṃ anugacchati || 8.29 ||
items.en: If the king passes over those Brahmins and wants to decide the matter himself, that sin grows a hundredfold and follows the king.

items.text:
प्रायश्चित्तं सदा दद्याद्देवतायतनाग्रतः ।
आत्मकृच्छ्रं ततः कृत्वा जपेद्वै वेदमातरम् ॥ ८.३० ॥
items.tr:
prāyaścittaṃ sadā dadyāddevatāyatanāgrataḥ |
ātmakṛcchraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā japedvai vedamātaram || 8.30 ||
items.en: Atonement should always be given in front of a temple. Then the man should perform a Kṛcchra himself and recite the Mother of the Vedas.
items.note: Kṛcchra: a penance of controlled eating and fasting over several days. 'Mother of the Vedas' is the Gāyatrī.

items.text:
सशिखं वपनं कृत्वा त्रिसंध्यं अवगाहनम् ।
गवां मध्ये वसेद्रात्रौ दिवा गाश्चाप्यनुव्रजेत् ॥ ८.३१ ॥
items.tr:
saśikhaṃ vapanaṃ kṛtvā trisaṃdhyaṃ avagāhanam |
gavāṃ madhye vasedrātrau divā gāścāpyanuvrajet || 8.31 ||
items.en: After shaving his whole head including the tuft, and bathing at dawn, noon and dusk, he should stay among the cows at night and follow them during the day.

items.text:
उष्णे वर्षति शीते वा मारुते वाति वा भृशम् ।
न कुर्वीतात्मनस्त्राणं गोरकृत्वा तु शक्तितः ॥ ८.३२ ॥
items.tr:
uṣṇe varṣati śīte vā mārute vāti vā bhṛśam |
na kurvītātmanastrāṇaṃ gorakṛtvā tu śaktitaḥ || 8.32 ||
items.en: In heat, rain, cold or strong wind, he should not shelter himself without first sheltering the cow as well as he can.

items.text:
आत्मनो यदि वान्येषां गृहे क्षेत्रे खलेऽथ वा ।
भक्षयन्तीं न कथयेत्पिबन्तं चैव वत्सकम् ॥ ८.३३ ॥
items.tr:
ātmano yadi vānyeṣāṃ gṛhe kṣetre khale'tha vā |
bhakṣayantīṃ na kathayetpibantaṃ caiva vatsakam || 8.33 ||
items.en: If a cow is eating in his own or someone else's house, field or threshing floor, he should not report it; nor should he report a calf that is drinking milk.

items.text:
पिबन्तीषु पिबेत्तोयं संविशन्तीषु संविशेत् ।
पतितां पङ्कमग्नां वा सर्वप्राणैः समुद्धरेत् ॥ ८.३४ ॥
items.tr:
pibantīṣu pibettoyaṃ saṃviśantīṣu saṃviśet |
patitāṃ paṅkamagnāṃ vā sarvaprāṇaiḥ samuddharet || 8.34 ||
items.en: He should drink water when the cows drink and lie down when they lie down. If one falls or sinks in mud, he should pull it out with all his strength.

items.text:
ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा यस्तु प्राणान्परित्यजेत् ।
मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्याया गोप्ता गोर्ब्राह्मणस्य च ॥ ८.३५ ॥
items.tr:
brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā yastu prāṇānparityajet |
mucyate brahmahatyāyā goptā gorbrāhmaṇasya ca || 8.35 ||
items.en: A man who gives up his life for the sake of a Brahmin or a cow is freed even from the sin of killing a Brahmin, as the protector of cow and Brahmin.

items.text:
गोवधस्यानुरूपेण प्राजापत्यं विनिर्दिशेत् ।
प्राजापत्यं ततः कृच्छ्रं विभजेत्तच्चतुर्विधं ॥ ८.३६ ॥
items.tr:
govadhasyānurūpeṇa prājāpatyaṃ vinirdiśet |
prājāpatyaṃ tataḥ kṛcchraṃ vibhajettaccaturvidhaṃ || 8.36 ||
items.en: For killing a cow, one should prescribe the Prājāpatya as fitting. The Prājāpatya Kṛcchra is divided into four parts.
items.note: Prājāpatya: a standard Kṛcchra penance in four equal stages: one meal by day, one meal at night, only food given unasked, and full fast.

items.text:
एकाहं एकभक्ताशी एकाहं नक्तभोजनः ।
अयाचिताश्येकं अहरेकाहं मारुताशनः ॥ ८.३७ ॥
items.tr:
ekāhaṃ ekabhaktāśī ekāhaṃ naktabhojanaḥ |
ayācitāśyekaṃ aharekāhaṃ mārutāśanaḥ || 8.37 ||
items.en: For one day he eats a single meal by day, for one day only at night, for one day only food he did not ask for, and for one day he lives on air.

items.text:
दिनद्वयं चैकभक्तो द्विदिनं चैकभोजनः ।
दिनद्वयं अयाची स्याद्द्विदिनं मारुताशनः ॥ ८.३८ ॥
items.tr:
dinadvayaṃ caikabhakto dvidinaṃ caikabhojanaḥ |
dinadvayaṃ ayācī syāddvidinaṃ mārutāśanaḥ || 8.38 ||
items.en: Or for two days he eats one meal by day, for two days one meal at night, for two days only unasked food, and for two days he lives on air.

items.text:
त्रिदिनं चैकभक्ताशी त्रिदिनं नक्तभोजनः ।
दिनत्रयं अयाची स्यात्त्रिदिनं मारुताशनः ॥ ८.३९ ॥
items.tr:
tridinaṃ caikabhaktāśī tridinaṃ naktabhojanaḥ |
dinatrayaṃ ayācī syāttridinaṃ mārutāśanaḥ || 8.39 ||
items.en: Or for three days he eats one meal by day, three days only at night, three days only unasked food, and three days he lives on air.
items.note: The text gives versions with one, two, three and four days per stage; it does not say here which length applies when.

items.text:
चतुरहं चैकभक्ताशी चतुरहं नक्तभोजनः ।
चतुर्दिनं अयाची स्याच्चतुरहं मारुताशनः ॥ ८.४० ॥
items.tr:
caturahaṃ caikabhaktāśī caturahaṃ naktabhojanaḥ |
caturdinaṃ ayācī syāccaturahaṃ mārutāśanaḥ || 8.40 ||
items.en: Or for four days he eats one meal by day, four days only at night, four days only unasked food, and four days he lives on air.

items.text:
प्रायश्चित्ते ततश्चीर्णे कुर्याद्ब्राह्मणभोजनम् ।
विप्राणां दक्षिणां दद्यात्पवित्राणि जपेद्द्विजः ॥ ८.४१ ॥
items.tr:
prāyaścitte tataścīrṇe kuryādbrāhmaṇabhojanam |
viprāṇāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadyātpavitrāṇi japeddvijaḥ || 8.41 ||
items.en: When the atonement is finished, he should feed Brahmins and give dakṣiṇā to them, and the twice-born man should recite purifying texts.
items.note: Dakṣiṇā: the gift or fee given to Brahmins at the end of a rite.

items.text: ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वा तु गोघ्नः शुद्धो न संशयः ॥ ८.४१.१ ॥
items.tr: brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā tu goghnaḥ śuddho na saṃśayaḥ || 8.41.1 ||
items.en: After feeding the Brahmins, the cow-killer is pure, without doubt.
